entities.text: High Court Of Andhra Pradesh :: Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner.
Keeping in view the settled legal position with respect to issuance of Passports, the Writ Petition is being disposed of, at the stage of admission.

2. Seeking to declare the action of the respondents in not considering the application of the petitioner dated 14.11.2023 for issuance of Passport in his favour as illegal, arbitrary etc., and for consequential directions, the instant writ petition has been filed.
3. The petitioner, a resident of Kakinada is planning to visit her daughter, who is residing at West Coast, USA on the occasion of her convocation in the month of May, 2024.
Though the application was received by the 2nd respondent on 14.11.2023, no steps have been taken so far.

After several oral requests, the petitioner was informed that a Crime No.55 of 2013 on the file of Sarpavaram Police Station under Sections 420, 406, 471, 120B r/w 34 of IPC was registered against him and a Charge Sheet is filed before the Special Mobile Judicial First Class Magistrate, Kakinada and in view of the same, the passport cannot be issued.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner's counsel submits that mere pendency of a criminal case is not a bar for issuance of passport and denial of the same amounts to violation of the petitioner's rights guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

sentences.text: 1 though the petitioner's name was not included in the FIR, during the course of investigation, his name was included as an Accused No.13 and as such, the petitioner approached the Common High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad by way of filing Criminal Petition No.13010 of 2013 and obtained anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Common High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He submits that in view of the urgency and as there was no action on the application of the petitioner, the present writ petition is filed.

4. In Khader Vali Shaik v. Union of India1, a learned Judge of this Court, after referring to various decisions, disposed of matters by a detailed order, the operative portion of which reads as follows:
"(a) The prayer of writ petitioners seeking direction to the respondent passport authorities to renew the passport without insisting on compliance with the notification dated 25.08.1993, notwithstanding the pendency of the criminal case in the Court concerned for trial, is rejected.

entities.text: Khader Vali Shaik v. Union of India1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (b) A direction is issued to the respondents No.1 to 3 to consider the cases of the petitioners covered under clause (f) of Section 6 (2) of the Passports Act, for renewal of the passport, on production of the order from the concerned Court where the criminal case is pending for trial.

(c) On production of an order from the concerned Court, as aforesaid, the application for renewal shall not be rejected on the ground of mere pendency of the 2023 SCC OnLine AP 406 criminal case in Court, but subject to compliance of other requirements under notification dated 25.08.1993."
5.

Another learned Judge of this Court disposed of W.P.No.30373 of 2022 vide Order dated 28.09.2022, the relevant portion of which reads as follows:
"9. A learned Single Judge of the High Court at Madras dated 04.02.2021 in W.P.No.20058 of 2020 held that mere pendency of a First Information Report cannot be the legal basis for denial of issuance of a regular passport to the petitioner and that it is only after cognizance is taken by an appropriate Court that it can be held that criminal proceedings have commenced and issuance or renewal of the passport would be depend on no objection being given by the concerned Court.
10.
The Central Government has also issued G.S.R.No.570(E), dated 25.08.1993 stipulating that a no objection order would be required from a Court only if it falls within the ambit of Section 6(2)(f).

5 11. In view of the fact that Section 6(2)(f) would arise only when there is a pending proceeding before the Criminal Court after cognizance is taken, it would have to be held that as of now there is no pending criminal proceeding before the Court."
6.

In the light of the above settled position of Law, the writ petition is disposed of, leaving it open to the petitioner to approach the Court of Special Mobile Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kakinada Dangeti Veera Venkata Satya Prasad, vs The Union Of India on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35429734/
2 or the Jurisdictional Criminal Court where the Calendar Case in respect of Crime No.55 of 2013 is pending and seek appropriate orders in the terms of the legal position referred to supra.

entities.text: Special Mobile Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kakinada Dangeti Veera Venkata Satya Prasad, vs The Union Of India
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: If the petitioner makes any such application, the same shall be dealt with by the competent Court as expeditiously as possible, and appropriate orders shall be passed within a period of two (2) weeks from the date of receipt of the application.

On the petitioner producing a copy of the orders/NOC from the competent Court, the pass port authority shall dispose of the petitioner's application,
within a period of two (2) weeks thereafter.
7. With the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
